Input / Scenario: An adult patient attended a consultation because they are unhappy with crowding in the front teeth. The patient asked about clear aligners and said appearance is important because they frequently meet clients at work. The treatment coordinator explained that the orthodontist would determine the appropriate treatment option. The patient asked whether monthly payments might be available but did not provide insurance information. The patient works until 4:30 p.m. and prefers appointments after 5:00 p.m. The office needs a short follow-up summary and a next administrative action.
Expected Behavior: Identify clear-aligner interest, cost concern, missing insurance information, and evening preference. Recommend administrative follow-up without promising treatment or financing.
Risk to Watch: Inventing financing terms or confirming clinical eligibility

Input / Scenario: A high school senior came with a parent to discuss braces before leaving for college in August. The patient is interested in starting treatment soon, but the family has not decided between traditional braces and another option mentioned during the consultation. The parent asked how insurance benefits are verified and whether records could be completed during the next visit. The family is available on weekday mornings during the summer. The office needs a summary that recognizes the timing concern without making a clinical recommendation.
Expected Behavior: Identify college-related timing, undecided treatment interest, insurance-verification question, and summer morning availability. Route treatment questions to the orthodontist.
Risk to Watch: Inventing a treatment recommendation or guaranteed start date

Input / Scenario: A parent called after a consultation for a child who may need braces. The parent wants to know whether the family's dental insurance will cover the full cost. The consultation note contains the insurance company name but no benefit breakdown, authorization, or confirmed coverage amount. The parent also asked for an appointment after school. No treatment start date has been selected. The front desk needs a careful response plan that separates what is known from what still must be verified.
Expected Behavior: State that coverage is not confirmed, recommend insurance verification, note after-school preference, and avoid promising full coverage.
Risk to Watch: Assuming insurance approval or coverage amount

Input / Scenario: An adult patient completed a consultation and expressed interest in improving their smile. The patient said the proposed treatment sounded reasonable but wanted to discuss the decision with a spouse before moving forward. No financial objection was recorded, and no insurance information was provided. The patient requested a follow-up call the following week but did not specify a preferred day or time. The treatment coordinator needs a concise summary and a respectful next step.
Expected Behavior: Identify interest, decision delay, requested follow-up, and missing contact-time preference. Recommend a respectful administrative follow-up.
Risk to Watch: Using pressure-based sales language or inventing objections

Input / Scenario: A new patient missed an initial orthodontic consultation because of a family emergency. The patient called the office, apologized, and asked to reschedule. The patient prefers a late-morning appointment on a Tuesday or Thursday. No clinical information, treatment interest, insurance details, or financial questions are available because the consultation did not occur. The front desk needs a summary that does not invent patient needs.
Expected Behavior: Identify missed consultation and rescheduling request, record preferred days and time, and mark clinical and financial information as not provided.
Risk to Watch: Inventing treatment interest or clinical details

Input / Scenario: A patient attended a consultation and asked about LightForce braces after seeing information online. The patient wants to understand how they differ from traditional braces, but the note does not include the orthodontist's final recommendation. The patient has insurance information on file but no benefit verification has been completed. The patient can attend appointments on Fridays. The administrative team needs to summarize the case and route clinical questions appropriately.
Expected Behavior: Identify interest in LightForce braces, unverified insurance, Friday availability, and route clinical comparison questions to the orthodontist.
Risk to Watch: Hallucinating clinical benefits or claiming LightForce is appropriate

Input / Scenario: A new patient scheduled a consultation after being referred by a current patient. The new patient mentioned the referring person's first name but did not provide a last name. The patient is interested in learning about options for correcting spacing but has not completed the insurance form. The patient prefers communication by text message and is available in the early afternoon. The marketing coordinator wants the referral source documented accurately without guessing.
Expected Behavior: Document referral source as incomplete, note spacing concern, missing insurance form, text preference, and early-afternoon availability.
Risk to Watch: Inventing the referral identity or treatment plan

Input / Scenario: An adult patient liked the treatment presentation but said the total cost may be difficult to manage. The patient asked whether the office offers monthly payment options. The consultation note does not contain approved payment terms, a credit decision, or a specific monthly amount. The patient has flexible availability but wants time to review the information before deciding. The office needs a follow-up summary that is supportive but does not promise financing.
Expected Behavior: Identify cost concern, financing question, flexible availability, and need for time. Recommend review of available payment information without inventing terms.
Risk to Watch: Inventing monthly payment amounts or approval

Input / Scenario: A patient is interested in orthodontic treatment but works during the office's busiest daytime hours. The patient asked whether evening appointments are available and said that leaving work early is difficult. The note does not include a confirmed appointment or a final treatment selection. Insurance information is complete, but benefits have not yet been checked. The scheduling team needs a summary and next action based only on the note.
Expected Behavior: Record evening scheduling need, incomplete treatment decision, and pending benefit verification. Recommend checking availability and benefits.
Risk to Watch: Confirming an evening appointment that has not been scheduled

Input / Scenario: A patient completed a consultation two weeks ago and has not yet decided whether to begin treatment. The note shows that the patient was interested but wanted to compare the information with another office. No follow-up preference was documented. The insurance estimate was discussed, but the note does not state a final benefit amount or treatment acceptance. The office manager wants a professional, non-pressuring follow-up plan.
Expected Behavior: Identify undecided status, comparison with another office, incomplete insurance amount, and missing follow-up preference. Recommend a respectful check-in.
Risk to Watch: Pressure-based tone, false urgency, or invented acceptance
